result.dataset: HOME corpus (pii-anon-eval-data v2.2.0) DEV split, language=en — 1200 seeded records (SEED=20260710, common.subsample) of 15510; strict exact scoring against LABEL_MAP-projected native predictions. Measured on this sample: vanilla P=0.8735 R=0.9022 F2=0.8963 (tp=7039 fp=1019 fn=763); swarm P=0.8669 R=0.9063 F2=0.8981 (tp=7071 fp=1086 fn=731).

fn_classes.name: bare coreferent mention of an introduced name
fn_classes.mechanism: A full PERSON_NAME is detected at first mention, but subsequent standalone mentions of one of its tokens (first-name-only 'Nancy', surname-only 'Flores', 'Jerry A.') are missed — no document-level mention propagation. Largest single FN class; shared with every prose dataset (external judgments/transcripts repeat surnames the same way).
examples: resolved the complaint. <<Nancy>> can be reached at +1 (486) 324-4086
Davis joined in 2020, while <<Jones>> joined in 2023
Colleagues, including Larry Thomas, praise <<Jerry A.>>'s collaborative approach
fn_classes.remediation: Document-level mention propagation: index tokens of accepted PERSON_NAME findings, re-scan the record for standalone token/initial mentions (incl. honorific+surname) and emit them as PERSON_NAME. Pure additive second pass, no new model.

fn_classes.name: suffix-less organization name in prose
fn_classes.mechanism: Org names without a legal-form anchor (no Inc/LLC/Corp) — 'Hooli', 'Dunder Mifflin', 'Weyland-Yutani', 'Pied Piper' — are either missed outright (56) or typed PERSON_NAME/LOCATION by the capitalized-phrase heuristics (38+), despite strong local cues ('employed at X', 'customer of X', 'Provider: X', case captions 'v. X', beneficiary/employer fields).
examples: I worked with Kevin Miller at <<Hooli>> for approximately 9 years
Kevin Thompson v. <<Pacific Northwest Tech>> - breach of contract [pred: PERSON_NAME]
fn_classes.remediation: Contextual ORG cue grammar: type the capitalized phrase ORGANIZATION when governed by employment/party/provider cues (at/against/v./Provider:/Employer:/beneficiary), and have that cue outrank the person-name reading in arbitration.

fn_classes.name: invisible-char injected value
fn_classes.mechanism: Zero-width/bidi characters inside value runs ('5598 3​397 970​1 5096', 'IN​V-​583829', '23​2379​6598') defeat the digit-run patterns. The sp3 invisible-char recovery covers only CVV/PIN/PASSWORD/INSURANCE/AUTH; CREDIT_CARD, BANK_ACCOUNT, INVOICE, TAX_ID, PERSON_NAME etc. still fail.
fn_classes.remediation: Generalize the offset-preserving invisible-char-strip + re-scan normalization pass to ALL entity classes instead of the sp3 five; gliner already recovers several of these pre-fusion.

fn_classes.name: encoded value in labeled field
fn_classes.mechanism: Base64-encoded values sitting after an explicit type label ('Bank Account Number: MDcyNjY2ODgyNw==', 'Cryptocurrency Address: MHg1OGNh…') and percent-encoded emails in URLs ('donald.brown13%40yahoo.com') are not decoded for types outside the sp3 tranche; when the decode probe does fire it can emit the wrong type (see FP arbitration class).
fn_classes.remediation: Extend base64/percent-decoding recovery to all labeled-field value classes and take the entity type from the field label, not from the decoded value's shape.

fn_classes.name: name-span boundary absorption/truncation
fn_classes.mechanism: The capitalized-run person pattern absorbs a preceding capitalized non-name token ('Email Nancy Young', 'User Nicholas Moore', 'Employees Betty Hernandez') or truncates long hyphenated/multi-part names ('Mary Catherine Elizabeth' vs gold '…O'Brien-Williams'); produces paired FN+FP under strict scoring. Swarm fixes 20 of these via gliner's exact spans.
examples: <<Email Joseph Johnson>> at joseph.johnson21@fastmail.com [gold: Joseph Johnson]
Patient <<Mary Catherine Elizabeth>> O'Brien-Williams [gold includes surname]
fn_classes.remediation: Leading-token stoplist (verbs/role nouns: Email/User/Employees/Contact/Usr) trimmed off name candidates + hyphen/apostrophe-aware surname-tail extension.

fn_classes.name: bare date in DOB-cue context
fn_classes.mechanism: ISO dates are emitted natively as DATE_ISO, which the projection deliberately drops as ambiguous — so gold DOBs with explicit cues ('My date of birth is 1952-07-12', 'you were born on…', DOB column in delimited rows) are all lost. The cue is present in nearly every miss.
examples: And you were born on <<1991-04-08>>, correct?
fn_classes.remediation: Context-conditioned DOB typing: emit DATE_OF_BIRTH (not DATE_ISO) when a birth cue ('born', 'DOB', 'date of birth') is within a small window or the value sits in a DOB-labeled field; keep uncued dates dropped.

fn_classes.name: labeled money amount (income field)
fn_classes.mechanism: Currency amounts under income labels ('Income: $46,000', 'annual income of $205,000', 'Combined income:') are missed — the SALARY pattern apparently needs the literal 'salary' cue. (Gold also labels 'Balance: $213,000' SALARY — partially gold-convention.)
examples: Client reports annual income of <<$205,000>> from Weyland-Yutani
fn_classes.remediation: Extend the SALARY cue lexicon to income/compensation/earnings (+labeled-field form); treat 'Balance:' as a corpus convention question for the dataset owner.

fn_classes.name: clinical condition after cue phrase
fn_classes.mechanism: Title-case disease names following clinical cues ('ASSESSMENT:', 'CC:', 'we're looking at', 'follow-up regarding') are missed by the condition lexicon (18) or typed PERSON_NAME because they look like capitalized bigrams (12: 'Acute Bronchitis', 'Major Depressive Disorder').
fn_classes.remediation: Condition lexicon/pattern expansion (standard ICD-style names incl. multiword Latinate forms) + suppress person-name candidates in clinical cue windows; directly attacks the HEALTH_CONDITION residual named in the brief.

fn_classes.name: job title in header/apposition
fn_classes.mechanism: Titles in resume-header apposition ('Melissa Garcia — Chief Technology Officer at Tyrell Corporation'), experience lines ('Research Scientist — Dunder Mifflin (2021–present)') and pluralized forms ('are both Network Administrators') are missed or typed PERSON_NAME. The JOB_TITLE residual from the brief is concentrated in these constructions.
examples: Melissa Garcia — <<Chief Technology Officer>> at Tyrell Corporation [pred: PERSON_NAME]
are both <<Network Administrator>>s at Oscorp Industries
fn_classes.remediation: Apposition grammar (NAME — TITLE at ORG; TITLE — ORG (dates)) + plural-tolerant title matching; title reading outranks person-name for phrases in these frames.

fn_classes.name: quoted credential in config/code form
fn_classes.mechanism: Credentials as quoted values in config/code ('DB_PASS = "RGupi7uNG@0ux84#"', 'dbUser: "admin_7268"') are missed — detection keys on prose cues, not key–value structure.
fn_classes.remediation: Key-name-driven key–value credential detector for config/JSON/env forms (pass/pwd/user/token/key aliases), typing from the key name. Same mechanism as the labeled-field classes — one seam.

fn_classes.name: typed-format value under generic label
fn_classes.mechanism: Passport-format values under a bare generic label ('ID: O43117599' in wire-transfer forms, gold=PASSPORT_NUMBER) and report-tag employee ids ('#TR-2970', gold=EMPLOYEE_ID) — the generator types generic IDs by their format, the detector requires a type-specific cue.
fn_classes.remediation: Format-shape fallback typing under generic 'ID:'-class labels is possible but this is substantially a generator convention (notary license as DL, report tag as employee id) — verify against TRAIN before adding patterns; do not chase the template anchors.

fn_classes.name: scheme-prefixed identifier span convention
fn_classes.mechanism: Gold includes the scheme prefix in the span ('MRN-4516037'), the detector emits the bare number ('4516037') — IoU≥0.5 same-type overlap in every case, so strict scoring books an FN+FP pair while relaxed forgives it.
fn_classes.remediation: Span-normalization: absorb a directly-attached ALLCAPS scheme prefix + hyphen into the emitted span (MRN-/INV-/POL-…). Cheap, purely convention-level strict-F2 win, no recall risk.

fn_classes.name: homoglyph-obfuscated identity text
fn_classes.mechanism: Cyrillic/Greek confusables inside names and emails ('Christорher Тhоmpson', 'steven.jacksоn13@protonmаil.сom') break both regex and tokenizer paths; swarm/gliner recovers 5 of them.
fn_classes.remediation: UTS#39 confusable-skeleton normalization pre-pass with offset re-basing (same seam as the invisible-char pass), applied before all engines.

fn_classes.name: OCR digit-letter confusion in checksummed id
fn_classes.mechanism: OCR-style letter-for-digit substitutions inside SSNs ('7B7-34-5883', 'S58-67-3725') fail the strict digit patterns; the swarm fixes all 5 via gliner.
examples: Scanned document: Patient Sandra Johnson, SSN <<7B7-34-5883>>
fn_classes.remediation: Extend the sp3 OCR-confusable map (the '8earer' precedent) to digit positions of SSN/checksummed patterns for the vanilla engine; swarm already covers it.

fn_classes.name: partially-masked value tail
fn_classes.mechanism: Redacted-prefix values with a live tail ('SSN: ***-**-8567', gold = last-4 only) are invisible to full-pattern regexes; the swarm detects them but disagrees with gold on span/type (see its FP twin).
fn_classes.remediation: Masked-prefix fragment patterns emitting fragment-typed findings with tail-only spans, matching the corpus last-4 convention (CREDIT_CARD_FRAGMENT already exists as a type precedent).

fn_classes.name: gold check-digit-invalid number
fn_classes.mechanism: Gold values that fail real-world validators: 3 Luhn-invalid 16-digit cards (0 of the plain missed cards were Luhn-valid — measured) and an SSA-invalid area-666 SSN. The detector's validators are correct; the generator emits invalid instruments.
fn_classes.remediation: Not fixable without weakening validators — report to the dataset owner; optionally demote Luhn/area checks from hard gate to confidence signal if the product philosophy prefers recall.

fn_classes.name: residual long-tail miss
fn_classes.mechanism: Mixed low-frequency mechanisms: medication form/dosage variants ('Albuterol Inhaler', 'Levothyroxine 75mcg'), federal docket formats ('11:26-mc-09749-VIL' after 'Case No:'), bare 5-digit postal codes in census rows, DL format variants ('D123-4567-8901'), label-glued values ('SSN<<575-35-7775>>' with no space), URL-with-PII path ids, prose-cued account numbers ('my account number is 8086385926'), and single categorical-type misses (the known sp3 categorical-to-filler cost).
examples: Patient Linda Jones's SSN<<575-35-7775>> was entered without a space
fn_classes.remediation: Individually small; the two general levers inside are (a) boundary-tolerant matching when a label is glued to the value, and (b) docket/case-number format union with the COURT_CASE/DOCKET disambiguation below.

fp_classes.name: title-case non-name phrase typed as person/entity
fp_classes.mechanism: The capitalized-phrase person heuristic fires on field labels ('Authentication Token:', 'Social Media Handle:', 'Court Reporter:'), document boilerplate ('United States District Judge', 'Certified Shorthand Reporter', 'Bar No.'), and section headers ('User Message', 'Fiscal Year') — 342 PERSON_NAME + 22 JOB_TITLE field-label hits. This is the single biggest precision lever (the PERSON_NAME fp≈5764 residual from the brief is mostly this class) and is prose-universal, so it transfers to every external dataset.
examples: EXAMINATION BY Brian Scott (<<Bar No>>. CA-281829)
Record for Ashley Perez, <<Authentication Token>>: QmVhcmVy…
fp_classes.remediation: Three stacked suppressors: (a) reject person candidates immediately followed by ':' (field-label position); (b) common-noun-pair filter — both tokens in an English common-word list ⇒ not a name; (c) small boilerplate/role stoplist (District/Reporter/Session/Message/Year…). All derivable from TRAIN.

fp_classes.name: gold under-annotation of true mentions
fp_classes.mechanism: Detector-correct findings the gold simply does not annotate: verified same-record repeat mentions of gold names (14 exact + 20 honorific/token-subset), all 28 MAC addresses in audit_log records, 23 'NN-year-old' ages, 31 medication repeat mentions in discharge prose, ~25 real job titles in witness statements ('employed at InGen as a Security Analyst'), 47 facility/org names in radiology/referral headers. Gold annotates bare mentions in some templates (FN side) and skips them in others (FP side) — inconsistent mention coverage.
examples: access from 52.235.78.112 (MAC: <<58:f8:ed:06:09:60>>) — audit_log gold has no MAC
We recommend promotion for <<Pamela Sanchez>> — same name gold-annotated twice elsewhere in the record
fp_classes.remediation: Not model-fixable; file against the corpus generator (mention-completeness for repeated names/meds/ages, MAC and facility annotation in audit_log/radiology templates). Roughly 17% of all FPs on both detectors — a hard precision ceiling on this split.

fp_classes.name: bare digit run typed as phone over labeled field
fp_classes.mechanism: 10-digit account numbers under explicit labels ('Bank Account:', 'Account:', 'acct') are captured by the bare-10-digit phone pattern, producing a PHONE FP over BANK_ACCOUNT gold (45) plus 23 spurious cousins.
fp_classes.remediation: Labeled-field arbitration: a field label naming a type outranks the bare-digit phone reading; require separators/punctuation or a phone cue for unlabeled 10-digit runs.

fp_classes.name: name-span boundary absorption (FP twin)
fp_classes.mechanism: FP half of the boundary FN class — over-extended person spans ('Email Nancy Young', 'Usr Linda Torres', 'Employees Betty Hernandez') and truncated long names; swarm adds 5 honorific-absorbed spans ('Dr. Ashley White' vs gold 'Ashley White').
examples: swarm: <<Dr. Ashley White>> [gold excludes the honorific]
fp_classes.remediation: Same fix as the FN class (leading-token stoplist + honorific convention alignment with gold: gold sometimes includes 'Ms. Sanchez' — pick one convention and normalize).

fp_classes.name: identifier span-convention disagreement
fp_classes.mechanism: Same-type overlapping spans that differ from gold by a scheme prefix or partial value (MRN digits-only vs 'MRN-…' — 20; other value boundary disagreements — 34): booked as FP+FN pairs under strict, forgiven under relaxed.
examples: 'Squamous' vs gold 'Squamous cell carcinoma in situ'
fp_classes.remediation: Prefix-absorbing span normalization + lexicon longest-match extension for multiword clinical terms.

fp_classes.name: pseudonymous handle deliberately not gold
fp_classes.mechanism: @handles heading paired_profile_pseudonymous records ('@midnight_sparrow386:') are detected as SOCIAL_MEDIA_HANDLE/USERNAME but intentionally carry no gold — the pseudonymous half of the pair is by design not annotated as PII.
fp_classes.remediation: Corpus-design convention, not a detector defect — masking a pseudonym is safe over-masking. Leave the detector alone; if strict-F2 on this split matters, raise the annotation policy question with the dataset owner.

fp_classes.name: NER engine types opaque fragment as location (swarm fusion gap)
fp_classes.mechanism: Swarm-only: the NER pool's GPE/LOC labels land on base64 blobs, EIN-shaped numbers and ID fragments ('NzctODE1MDg3Ng', '41-5751348', 'NID-38Z036310') and fusion passes them through — 46 of the swarm's 67 net-new FPs.
fp_classes.remediation: Fusion-side plausibility gate for LOC-typed findings: must contain an alphabetic word token and not be digit/symbol-majority; drop NER LOC findings that overlap a labeled value field.

fp_classes.name: labeled-field type arbitration loss (tax-id as national-id)
fp_classes.mechanism: EIN-format values under an explicit 'Tax ID:' label are typed NATIONAL_ID_NUMBER (27), including cases where the base64/zero-width recovery correctly finds the value but then types it by shape instead of by the field label; siblings: HEALTH_INSURANCE_ID→NATIONAL_ID (4), reverse TAX_ID→NATIONAL_ID confusions (5).
examples: Tax Id: <<NzctODE1MDg3Ng>>== recovered but typed NATIONAL_ID
Tax Id: <<18-3085>>​51​5 recovered but typed NATIONAL_ID
fp_classes.remediation: Field-label-driven type override in arbitration (one rule shared with the phone/account class and the encoded-value FN class — a single 'label wins' seam fixes all three).

fp_classes.name: slash-date fragment typed as coordinates
fp_classes.mechanism: The MM/DD prefix of US-format dates ('Date of Birth: 05/21/2003') matches the slash-separated numeric-pair coordinate pattern, emitting LATITUDE_LONGITUDE over DATE_OF_BIRTH gold and simultaneously losing the DOB.
examples: What is your date of birth? A: <<10/02>>/1968
fp_classes.remediation: Coordinate pattern must require decimal degrees, sign/direction markers, or comma-separated pair form; reject candidates embedded inside a longer date token.

fp_classes.name: court-number taxonomy split (case vs docket)
fp_classes.mechanism: The same federal-format string is emitted COURT_CASE_NUMBER where gold says DOCKET_NUMBER — a taxonomy-boundary disagreement between two sibling types, paired with 6 DOCKET FNs.
fp_classes.remediation: Disambiguate by cue ('Docket No.' vs 'Case No.') or, if the corpus treats them interchangeably, alias at the projection layer — decide from TRAIN counts.

fp_classes.name: masked-tail span disagreement (swarm)
fp_classes.mechanism: Swarm-only twin of the masked-value FN class: gliner detects redacted SSNs but emits the whole masked span ('***-**-9985') or a different fragment ('8670') than gold's last-4 convention — 12-14 net-new swarm FPs.
examples: swarm pred '<<8670>>' offset from gold tail
vanilla has no finding at all here (FN)
fp_classes.remediation: Post-fusion span normalization to the tail-only fragment convention when a finding overlaps a masked prefix ('***').

fp_classes.name: negative-context honeypot ignored
fp_classes.mechanism: Deliberate trap values with explicit negation ('Order #123-45-6789 was shipped (not an SSN)', 'Product SKU: 4532-1234-5678-9012 (not a credit card)', 'Conference room 10.0.0.1 (room number, not IP)') are still emitted — no negative-context suppression exists.
fp_classes.remediation: Negation-cue suppressor: parenthetical/trailing 'not a(n) <type>' or a conflicting type label (SKU/Order #/room) within a short window demotes the finding. NOTE the sp2 leak-direction rule: implement as an EVAL/REPORT-side demotion or confidence downgrade, never as a silent drop on the production masking path.

fp_classes.name: cue-word-adjacent common token typed as username
fp_classes.mechanism: The 'User X' proximity heuristic captures the ordinary next word: 'User <<profile>>:', '[USER <<INPUT>>]' in prompt-injection scaffolding — the candidate has no value shape at all.
fp_classes.remediation: Value-shape constraint on username candidates: require digit/underscore/mixed-case or OOV token; plain dictionary words after 'user' are rejected.

fp_classes.name: unannotated quoted-thread and prose repeat mentions
fp_classes.mechanism: Emails inside quoted reply headers ('--- Original Message --- From: Maria Jackson <maria.jackson33@protonmail.com>') and disease repeat mentions in narrative ('was first diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis') are detected but carry no gold — same under-annotation family as the main gold-noise class, kept separate because it is concentrated in email-thread and longitudinal-record templates.
examples: From: Maria Jackson <<<maria.jackson33@protonmail.com>>> [quoted thread, no gold]
was first diagnosed with <<Rheumatoid Arthritis>> on 2022-06-10 [no gold]
fp_classes.remediation: Dataset report; detector behavior is correct (quoted-thread PII is real PII).

fp_classes.name: residual low-frequency confusions
fp_classes.mechanism: Mixed remainder: CC last-4 fragments typed as full CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER instead of CREDIT_CARD_FRAGMENT, ORGANIZATION↔LOCATION facility-vs-place flips, LICENSE_PLATE→DRIVER_LICENSE, spurious PROCEDURE/INSURANCE/CREDIT_CARD_FRAGMENT hits in templated rows, USERNAME→PERSON confusions.
fp_classes.remediation: Fragment-type routing for last-4 patterns is the only sub-class above ~10 instances; rest is long tail — do not chase individually.

result.swarm_delta_note: Swarm is strictly additive over vanilla on this sample: it fixes 32 vanilla FNs (20 PERSON_NAME — mostly exact-span recoveries of boundary-absorbed names via gliner; 7 SSN including all 5 OCR-confusables '7B7-34-5883'-style plus the area-666 one; 5 homoglyph emails) and introduces ZERO new FNs, but adds 67 FPs: 46 LOCATION_NAME on opaque fragments (base64 blobs, EIN-shaped numbers, 'NID-…' ids — the NER pool's GPE/LOC labels passed through fusion unfiltered), 14 SSN masked-tail span disagreements, 5 honorific-absorbed person spans ('Dr. Ashley White'). Net strict: P 0.8735→0.8669, R 0.9022→0.9063, F2 0.8963→0.8981. GLINER-PREFUSION SAMPLE (windowed GLiNERAdapter run directly on 71 swarm-FN records): 30 gold spans are found by raw gliner but ABSENT from the fused swarm output — PERSON_NAME 13 (incl. 'Johann Sebastian von Hohenberg' at conf 0.95, zero-width 'James ‍Rodrigue​z' at 0.57, bare first names ~0.54), BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER 4 (zero-width and base64 forms, conf up to 0.81), DATE_OF_BIRTH 4 (ISO date conf 0.93), EMAIL 3 (percent-encoded conf 0.79), STREET_ADDRESS 2, PASSPORT 2, CC 1, USERNAME 1. Fusion is discarding genuine single-engine gliner findings even at 0.93-0.95 confidence — a confidence-tiered single-engine acceptance path (accept lone gliner findings above a TRAIN-derived threshold, at least for PERSON/DOB/EMAIL) is the most concrete measured fusion lever; it directly overlaps the invisible-char, encoded-value and homoglyph FN classes. Cross-dataset intersection: the classes most likely shared with the external datasets (hence the most general levers) are bare-coreferent mentions, title-case-phrase person FPs, suffix-less org names, name-boundary absorption, and labeled-field type arbitration — all prose-mechanism classes with no home-template dependency.
result.gold_noise_note: Measured gold noise on this split cuts both directions. FP side: ~202 FPs/detector (~20% of vanilla's 1019) are verifiable under-annotation — 34 repeat/honorific mentions of names that ARE gold elsewhere in the same record (verified by same-record string match; e.g. a third 'Pamela Sanchez' mention unannotated while two others are gold), all 28 MAC addresses in audit_log records (template annotates no MACs at all), 23 'NN-year-old' age phrases, 31 medication repeat mentions, ~25 genuine job titles in witness statements, 47 facility names in radiology/referral headers, plus 32-34 quoted-email-thread addresses and prose condition repeat mentions. FN side: 5 gold values fail real-world validators (3 Luhn-invalid credit cards — 0 of the plainly-missed cards were Luhn-valid — and an SSA-invalid area-666 SSN), and 46 pseudonymous @handles are deliberately not gold by paired-profile design. Mention-level annotation is INCONSISTENT across templates: gold demands bare coreferent mentions in performance-review/clinical templates (150 FNs) while omitting identical mention types in others (34+ FPs), so any mention-propagation fix will trade some of the FN class for new FPs on the under-annotated templates — worth flagging to the eval-data owner before tuning against this split; a mention-completeness pass on the generator would firm up both scores.

result.dataset: ai4privacy-400k validation/1en via ds_ai4privacy400k.py (seeded common.subsample SEED=20260710, cap 1200 -> 1200 records, 1436 gold spans; rates cross-check the recorded 5000-record runs: van strict R 0.170 vs 0.1675, swm 0.200 vs 0.1987)

fn_classes.name: rare-name-out-of-lexicon
fn_classes.mechanism: Single-token person names with rare/non-Anglo stems (often after a form label 'Name:'/'Student:' or in greeting position) produce no PERSON_NAME hit at all — name recall is lexicon/shape-driven and unknown stems never fire. GLiNER pre-fusion finds 150/208 GIVENNAME golds but only 63 survive fusion.
examples: Mrs <<Möllering>>, let's implement a wellness week
fn_classes.remediation: Capitalized-token-after-name-cue rule (name-labeled fields, salutation position); accept single-engine GLiNER PERSON_NAME findings in fusion (see swarm note) instead of requiring corroboration.

fn_classes.name: name-span-convention-split
fn_classes.mechanism: Dataset splits names into GIVENNAME+SURNAME single tokens; our PERSON_NAME emits full-name (or salutation-absorbed) spans projected onto GIVENNAME only, so SURNAME golds become cross-type hits and GIVENNAME golds fail strict/IoU on boundaries.
examples: gold SURNAME <<Kandil>> vs pred GIVENNAME 'Miss Kandil'
fn_classes.remediation: Mostly scoring convention (not a bug); the real fix inside it: strip salutations/honorifics from span starts, and optionally emit first/last sub-spans alongside the full-name span.

fn_classes.name: unmarked-username-token
fn_classes.mechanism: Handle-shaped tokens without an @-sigil or explicit cue (dot-joined pairs, digit-affixed scrambles) in prose/greeting position never fire; USERNAME pattern needs sigil/label. Even explicit 'Username:' fields miss when the value is bare. GLiNER finds 43/135 pre-fusion, 9 survive.
examples: <<asparuh.olchawa>>, please make sure all media files...
Hi <<43ece>>, physical therapy sessions covered by...
fn_classes.remediation: Handle-shape heuristic (non-dictionary lowercase token with digit affix or dot-joined pair) gated on soft context (user/login/client/greeting); labeled-field value extractor for 'Username:' forms.

fn_classes.name: bare-numeric-identifier-untyped
fn_classes.mechanism: Variable-length digit strings (6-24 digits) with no checksum or format signature (IDCARDNUM, ACCOUNTNUM) are only typable from adjacent context nouns ('ID Card:', 'Account #', 'Payment authorized using'), which the format-only patterns never consume; ~13% of all pure misses sit directly after an explicit field label. GLiNER found 15 IDCARDNUM golds pre-fusion — 0 survived fusion.
fn_classes.remediation: New capability: labeled-field value extractor (field-name lexicon -> entity type applied to the following token) + a generic opaque-digit-identifier type that context re-types.

fn_classes.name: place-name-gap-or-typed-as-person
fn_classes.mechanism: City/town names outside the LOCATION vocabulary miss entirely (74), and capitalized multiword place names default to PERSON_NAME (45 detected-but-mistyped). The GLiNER adapter's _PII_LABELS has no city/location label at all (0 CITY preds pre-fusion), so the swarm cannot help.
fn_classes.remediation: Add a location/city label to the GLiNER label set (one-line config); GB/US town gazetteer; person-vs-place arbitration using context prepositions (in/at, residence verbs).

fn_classes.name: nonstandard-separator-digit-groups
fn_classes.mechanism: Phone/SSN grammars accept canonical separators only; mixed dot/space/paren groupings and unusual group splits miss ('+448.49.228.2855', '(652)-0742686', SSN '179.03.7418'). The one FN area the swarm genuinely improves (phone 46->30, SSN 18->12) via presidio/gliner corroboration.
fn_classes.remediation: Separator-agnostic normalization: collapse [.\s()-] runs and match on the digit-group skeleton, then re-project offsets.

fn_classes.name: digit-identifier-family-surface-collision
fn_classes.mechanism: Format-identical surfaces across identifier families get the wrong label: detected but typed as another digit type (IDCARDNUM '244559832' -> SOCIALNUM; IDCARDNUM '19337316545' -> TELEPHONENUM). Includes 18 TAXNUM golds in exact SSN format — structurally unseparable (dataset quirk, same surface).
fn_classes.remediation: Context-noun re-typing near digit spans (tax/passport/account/ID lexicon outranks bare format); the TAXNUM-vs-SOCIALNUM subset (18) is gold-structural — not fixable.

fn_classes.name: building-number-unreachable
fn_classes.mechanism: Dataset splits postal addresses into STREET+BUILDINGNUM+CITY+ZIPCODE; BUILDINGNUM (bare house numbers) has no native counterpart by design and is disclosed unreachable in the adapter mapping.
examples: authorize care at <<3397>> Bure Lane, Didcot
fn_classes.remediation: Convention: emitting a standalone house-number type would be noise-positive in production; leave disclosed-unreachable.

fn_classes.name: gb-postcode-locale-gap
fn_classes.mechanism: ZIP pattern covers US 5-digit only; GB full postcodes ('CT6 6JL'), outward-only forms ('BS1', 'WV14'), and some ZIP+4 miss. Pure locale coverage gap on the GB half of the split.
fn_classes.remediation: Add GB postcode grammar (outward [A-Z]{1,2}\d[A-Z\d]? + optional inward) as a locale-conditioned pattern; derivable from public spec, no dataset lexicon needed.

fn_classes.name: generic-date-not-promoted-to-dob
fn_classes.mechanism: 35 textual/ordinal dates ('2nd October 2009') miss the narrow native DATE_OF_BIRTH pattern, and 24 more ARE detected natively as DATE_TIME which the honest projection drops (DATE_TIME->None) — the detector never uses adjacent DOB cues ('DOB:', 'Date of Birth:', 'born on') to promote a generic date. GLiNER hits 44/69 pre-fusion; 9 survive.
examples: Date of Birth: <<2nd October 2009>> (DATE_TIME found, dropped)
born on <<17th May 1988>> (gliner hit, fusion discarded)
fn_classes.remediation: Cue-window promotion: re-type DATE_TIME/DATE_ISO to DATE_OF_BIRTH when a DOB cue is within ~30 chars; also extend textual-date grammar (ordinal day + month name).

fn_classes.name: street-name-only-span
fn_classes.mechanism: ADDRESS detection anchors on house-number+street composites; street-name-only spans ('Fig Tree Road') under the dataset's STREET/BUILDINGNUM split don't fire. Part convention (split spans), part real gap (road-suffix vocabulary). GLiNER finds 40/50 pre-fusion (ADDRESS label), 7 survive.
examples: recorded by Jared at <<Montgomery Dam Road>>, Potter
fn_classes.remediation: Street-suffix-anchored detection (Road/Street/Lane/Close/Drive/Boulevard...) emitting a street-grain sub-span alongside the composite ADDRESS.

fn_classes.name: credential-secret-without-cue
fn_classes.mechanism: Short high-entropy mixed-class tokens referenced by credential verbs ('log in with your new BE{4tv', 'use X for login') miss — PASSWORD pattern needs an explicit label. WARNING: GLiNER alone hits 30/44 but with 302 password preds (alone-precision 0.10), so blanket ML acceptance would crater precision.
fn_classes.remediation: Entropy+character-class token detector strictly gated on a credential-verb/noun context window (password/login/credentials/validate using).

fn_classes.name: license-format-family-gap
fn_classes.mechanism: Driver-license coverage is a small set of US formats; GB DVLA-style (SURNAME5+digits, spaced or hyphenated groups) and other alphanumeric families miss. GLiNER finds 16/32 pre-fusion, 5 survive.
fn_classes.remediation: Add DVLA-shaped grammar (from public spec) + license-context typing for otherwise-opaque alphanumerics after 'license #'.

fn_classes.name: checksum-rejecting-scrambled-pan-gold
fn_classes.mechanism: CREDITCARDNUMBER golds are scrambled placeholders that fail Luhn (or are 17-19 digit non-PAN shapes); a correct Luhn-validating detector cannot reach them. The 'Card Number:'-labeled subset would be recovered by the labeled-field extractor, not by weakening the validator.
fn_classes.remediation: Not fixable at the validator (gold noise); labeled-field extraction recovers the explicitly-labeled subset honestly.

fp_classes.name: titlecase-heading-as-person-name
fp_classes.mechanism: The capitalized-word-sequence PERSON_NAME heuristic fires on section headings, form labels, and Title-Case common-noun phrases (316/369 are multiword Title-Case); eval cross-type arbitration only drops job-title/org/condition overlaps, not generic headings. Biggest single precision killer (~40% of all strict FPs).
fp_classes.remediation: Common-vocabulary veto (all tokens in a frequent-English list -> reject) + field-label position veto (Title-Case phrase immediately followed by ':' is a field NAME, not a value).

fp_classes.name: proper-noun-family-confusion
fp_classes.mechanism: No person/place/org disambiguation for capitalized phrases: multiword city names predicted as GIVENNAME (57 cross-type onto CITY/STREET gold), and person/bank/org names predicted as LOCATION (38 spurious CITY).
fp_classes.remediation: Family-level arbitration using context (in/at prepositions and residence verbs -> place; greeting/salutation -> person; corporate suffixes Bank/Inc/LLC -> org, drop).

fp_classes.name: salutation-absorbed-name-span
fp_classes.mechanism: Greeting/honorific tokens ('Hey', 'Dear Miss', 'Mstr', 'Madame', 'Greetings') are capitalized and adjacent, so PERSON_NAME absorbs them; the widened span fails strict everywhere and drops below IoU 0.5 for short names, manufacturing paired FP+FN. 44-47 of these are salutation-prefixed; the rest are full-name vs single-token-gold convention.
fp_classes.remediation: Salutation/honorific strip-list applied to PERSON_NAME span starts — a genuinely general span-hygiene fix; remainder is scoring convention.

fp_classes.name: document-serial-as-phone
fp_classes.mechanism: All 76 FPs are the same shape: an alphabetic document prefix glued to 20YYMM-NNNN ('REF-201802-3893', 'TRANS-201310-2251'); the phone grammar accepts the 6-4 digit grouping and ignores the attached uppercase prefix token.
fp_classes.remediation: Left-boundary guard: reject phone candidates glued to an [A-Z]{2,}- prefix; veto leading digit group that parses as 20YY MM.

fp_classes.name: luhn-colliding-device-id-as-card
fp_classes.mechanism: 50/56 are 15-digit strings — IMEIs are Luhn-valid 15-digit numbers, so checksum cannot separate them from PANs (11 have explicit 'IMEI' context labels the detector ignores).
fp_classes.remediation: Negative-context veto (IMEI/serial/device) + constrain 15-digit PANs to Amex IIN prefixes (34/37) — both general, spec-derivable.

fp_classes.name: bare-9-digit-as-ssn
fp_classes.mechanism: US_SSN accepts unseparated 9-digit strings regardless of context; the bare-9-digit space is dense with other identifiers (16/43 sit in explicit passport context; others are account/id numbers).
fp_classes.remediation: Require separators (3-2-4) OR positive SSN/social context for bare 9 digits; negative-context veto on passport/routing.

fp_classes.name: digit-identifier-cross-label
fp_classes.mechanism: Mirror of the FN collision class: digit spans overlap gold of a sibling type (SOCIALNUM pred on TAXNUM gold 19 — structural same-surface; phone pred on SOCIALNUM/ACCOUNTNUM/IDCARDNUM gold; CREDITCARDNUMBER pred on ACCOUNTNUM/IDCARDNUM gold).
fp_classes.remediation: Same context-noun re-typing as the FN class; the 19 SSN-surface TAXNUM collisions are gold-structural (unfixable in-format).

fp_classes.name: cue-adjacent-common-word-as-username
fp_classes.mechanism: The USERNAME context rule grabs the token following 'user'/'login' even when it is a plain dictionary word (23/39 are bare lowercase words: 'history', 'agent', 'social').
fp_classes.remediation: Dictionary-word veto on cue-driven username candidates unless the token has handle evidence (digits, dots, mixed case).

fp_classes.name: unvalidated-iban-shape
fp_classes.mechanism: IBAN pattern matches CC+2digits+alphanumerics without mod-97 validation or a country whitelist, so VINs ('XB569W7R4UWDBARA5'), US-prefixed pseudo-IBANs (US has no IBAN), and unlabeled filler IBANs all fire.
fp_classes.remediation: Add mod-97 checksum + IBAN-country-code whitelist (spec-derivable); the labeled-IBAN subset is partly gold noise (true IBANs the dataset left unannotated).

result.swarm_delta_note: Swarm differs from vanilla only where regex corroborates an ML hit: strict TP 244->287 (+43, concentrated in TELEPHONENUM pure-miss 46->30, SOCIALNUM 18->12, name-boundary improvements) at +17 strict FPs (921->938). The dominant measured finding is the fusion discard: GLiNER pre-fusion relaxed-hits 597/1436 gold spans (1520 mapped preds; alone P=0.393, R=0.416) but only 298 survive SwarmFusionStrategy; the fused swarm ends at 346 relaxed TPs (P=0.282, R=0.241) — GLiNER alone dominates the fused swarm on BOTH precision and recall on this prose dataset. Mechanism located in src/pii_anon/swarm.py Layer 4: (a) SEMANTIC_TYPES corroboration gate (corroboration_min=2, override 0.85) is structurally unreachable for single-engine candidates because the logistic fallback caps a non-regex single-engine meta_score at sigmoid(2*ds_conf-1.5)<=0.62; (b) emission_threshold=0.50 kills most single-engine non-semantic candidates too (IDCARDNUM 15 gliner hits -> 0 survive; DRIVERLICENSENUM 16->5); (c) DS/type-vote flips DATE_OF_BIRTH clusters to DATE_TIME, which the projection honestly drops. Per-label discards (hit_pre->survived): GIVENNAME 150->63, TELEPHONENUM 74->42, DATEOFBIRTH 44->9, STREET 40->7, USERNAME 43->9, PASSWORD 30->4, CREDITCARDNUMBER 24->11; EMAIL 121->121 and SOCIALNUM 24->23 survive only because regex corroborates. Remediation: per-(engine,type) acceptance priors for single-engine findings instead of the blanket semantic gate — accept gliner-only name/street/dob/username/phone (alone-precision ~0.4), keep gating gliner-only PASSWORD (alone-precision 0.10, 302 preds/30 hits). Also add a location label to the GLiNER adapter's _PII_LABELS (it currently emits zero city/location findings).
result.gold_noise_note: Measured gold-noise strata, kept out of capability classes: (1) TAXNUM vs SOCIALNUM share the exact SSN surface ('181-01-0747') — 18 FN + 19 FP per detector are structurally undecidable; (2) scrambled placeholder values occupy semantically wrong slots ('Dr. wsgqnpedll06819' is USERNAME gold in a doctor-name position; 'Hi <<04/06/2018>>' is a DOB gold in a greeting slot), so context-driven detection is actively punished; (3) ~15 CREDITCARDNUMBER golds are non-Luhn/17-19-digit scrambles unreachable by a correct Luhn validator; (4) list-valued single gold spans ('SY13 2RN, SY13 2RP, SY13 2RW' as one ZIPCODE); (5) month/2-digit DOB golds ('May/18', 'October/23'); (6) unannotated true PII in text (filler IBANs, template residue '[ USERNAME_35 ]' where the FP 'NAME_35' is a template artifact). Rough share: ~4-6% of FN mass and ~5% of FP mass is gold-noise-dominated; the rest is genuine capability/convention signal.

result.dataset: nemotron — nvidia/Nemotron-PII test split (locale=us, 50,000 records), seeded 1200-record subsample via common.subsample(SEED=20260710); both detectors run zero-shot; failure sets mined under the relaxed criterion (same mapped label, IoU>=0.5, greedy 1:1). Totals: vanilla tp=3306 fp=8306 fn=6966; swarm tp=3311 fp=8348 fn=6961. Only the test parquet is local — any lexicon/threshold proposed below must be derived from the upstream TRAIN split (not yet downloaded).

fn_classes.name: split-token-name-convention
fn_classes.mechanism: We emit full-name PERSON_NAME spans; Nemotron gold splits first_name/last_name into single tokens, so 'Julio Wachtel' vs gold 'Julio' has IoU 0.385 and fails even relaxed matching — the same span is simultaneously an FN and an FP. last_name is additionally unreachable (1:1 pred_map already consumed by first_name).
examples: On 09/15/2024, <<Julio>> Wachtel, who lives at 312 Shepard Rd (gold first_name; our PERSON_NAME covers 'Julio Wachtel', IoU 0.385)
On 2023-10-22, Roberto <<Perez>>, a hispanic sales representative (gold last_name; PERSON_NAME overlap IoU 0.385)
Julio <<Wachtel>>, who lives at... (gold last_name, PERSON_NAME IoU 0.538 — barely passes only when name is 2 short tokens)
fn_classes.remediation: Match-time/emission convention, not detection: emit component sub-spans (given/family) alongside the full-name span, or give the eval adapter sub-span credit. Recurs on any corpus with token-split name gold.

fn_classes.name: single-token-name-not-recognized
fn_classes.mechanism: The person recognizers require multi-token Title-Case (PERSON_FULL_NAME = two+ capitalized words) or a context keyword; a lone given or family name in a labeled form field ('First Name: Julio') or prose appositive ('I, Donald, born on...') never fires. GLiNER finds many of these pre-fusion but fusion discards them.
examples: I, <<Donald>>, born on 2001-01-08, confirm that I am eligible to vote
When asked about her cultural practices, <<Melissa>> mentioned that she enjoys...
fn_classes.remediation: Labeled-field name capture (a 'first/last/name' field label licenses a single Title-Case token as the value) + let fusion admit gliner single-token name spans (see swarm note).

fn_classes.name: labeled-value-adjacency-broken (markdown/copula/appositive/xml)
fn_classes.mechanism: Cue AND value are both present but the cue-gated pattern requires immediate 'cue [:\-]? value' adjacency; inline markdown decoration ('**Account Number:** 4927136580'), a copula/preposition ('routing number of 093108495', 'password should be River2023$'), an appositive comma ('your new PIN, 1462, to complete'), or XML tags ('<accountNumber>231215-198726</accountNumber>') sit between cue and value. Measured sub-counts (vanilla): markdown 291, copula/preposition 230, appositive comma 90, xml 3.
examples: - **Account Number:** <<4927136580>> - **Customer ID:** 23CUST45681 (BANK_ACCOUNT needs 'account...:' then digits; ':**' breaks the bridge)
with a bank routing number of <<093108495>> ('of' between cue and value)
Click the link and enter your new PIN, <<1462>>, to complete the recovery (appositive)
fn_classes.remediation: One shared tolerant label-to-value bridge for ALL cue-gated patterns: strip/skip inline decoration ('**','__') and allow an optional copula/preposition token ('is|was|of|:') — or an offset-preserving markup-normalization pre-pass. Single change lifts account/routing/employee/MRN/PIN/password/user_name simultaneously; recurs on any markdown/form/XML corpus.

fn_classes.name: cue-vocabulary-or-value-class-too-narrow
fn_classes.mechanism: The type exists natively but either (a) the dataset's cue phrase is missing from the pattern ('health plan beneficiary number' vs our 'insurance'; 'Postcode:' vs 'zip|postal code'; 'User ID' vs 'username|login|handle'), or (b) the value class is narrower than real formats: BANK_ACCOUNT is digits-only \d{8,17} vs 'FR76 2000 1090 1234 5678 90', '231215-198726', 'C92871356'; API_KEY needs 32+ chars and a [:=-] separator vs 16-char keys and comma-separated UUIDs; GPS is signed-decimal-pair-only vs '40.7234 N, 123.1235 W'.
examples: the health plan beneficiary number <<WA-0003245789>> (cue word entirely absent from HEALTH_INSURANCE pattern; 114 FNs)
City: Crandall | State: GA | Postcode: <<30711>> (single-word 'Postcode' cue not in ZIP_CODE pattern)
The brokerage account number is <<1234-5678-9012-3456>> (hyphenated; value class digits-only)
fn_classes.remediation: Per-type cue-synonym expansion + value-class widening (allow letters, hyphens, spaced groups behind a strong cue) — derive the synonym/format inventory from the Nemotron TRAIN split (must be downloaded; only test is local). Hemisphere-suffixed coordinate format is a concrete missing pattern.

fn_classes.name: categorical-demographic-in-prose
fn_classes.mechanism: gender/race/education/politics/religion/sexuality/age appear as common words inside prose ('a female colleague', 'holds a bachelor's degree', lowercase values) with no field label; our categorical recognizers are deliberately label-gated ('Gender: Male') because bare lexicon words are FP bombs — the documented sp3 accepted cost, re-confirmed here.
examples: reported that a <<female>> colleague had been denied a promotion
The sales representative, who holds a <<bachelor's degree>> (lowercase; pattern requires capitalized Bachelor)
- **Education Level**: <<Some college>> (value not in lexicon even with label present)
fn_classes.remediation: Only safely fixable via a semantic engine (gliner labels for demographics) admitted by fusion in prose contexts, plus lexicon additions for labeled forms ('Some college', lowercase degree variants). Do not un-gate the bare lexicon.

fn_classes.name: free-text-occupation
fn_classes.mechanism: Occupations in prose are lowercase common-noun phrases ('sales representative', 'woodworker', 'first line supervisor of retail...'); JOB_TITLE has only a ~20-entry Title-Case lexicon + a labeled form. A further 98 FNs are Title-Case occupations detected but as PERSON_NAME (cross-type confusion).
examples: Roberto Perez, a hispanic <<sales representative>>, emailed his supervisor
Meet Jane, a dedicated <<sales representative wholesale or manufacturing>>
fn_classes.remediation: NER-shaped gap: occupation is an open class; regex lexicons cannot enumerate it. Route to gliner/NER 'occupation' label via fusion; optionally an appositive frame ('a/an <occ> who/,') gated on a train-derived occupation head-noun list.

fn_classes.name: geo-granularity-taxonomy-gap (state/county/country)
fn_classes.mechanism: Native taxonomy has one LOCATION type (mapped to city); state, county, country gold (712 spans) has no native counterpart at all — unreachable by any mapping, not a pattern failure.
fn_classes.remediation: New capability: split LOCATION into city/state/county/country subtypes (labeled-field + gazetteer for states/countries is cheap and high-precision). Counties also drive PERSON_NAME FPs ('Hays County'), so one gazetteer serves both directions.

fn_classes.name: misc-unreachable-types (time/date_time/customer_id/unique_id/http_cookie/employment_status/language/blood_type)
fn_classes.mechanism: Eight Nemotron types have no native counterpart: time (264), date_time (188), customer_id (215), unique_id (25), http_cookie (61), employment_status (143), language (104), blood_type (60). Structural taxonomy scope, not detection failure; customer_id/unique_id are generic-identifier classes we deliberately lack.
examples: identifies as white... blood type of <<O+>>
fn_classes.remediation: Taxonomy decision, not a pattern fix: add GENERIC_CUSTOMER_ID/TIME/BLOOD_TYPE etc. only if product scope wants them; labeled-field capture would get customer_id/unique_id nearly free once the shared cue-bridge exists.

fn_classes.name: generic-url-vs-pii-url-subset
fn_classes.mechanism: URL_WITH_PII fires only on URLs carrying PII (semantic subset by design); Nemotron's url type is any URL, so plain URLs (500 spans) are structurally missed. Documented zero-shot mapping decision, not a regression.
fn_classes.remediation: Convention: if generic-URL coverage is wanted, add a plain URL type (trivial pattern) kept distinct from URL_WITH_PII so masking policy can differ; otherwise accept the capped recall.

fn_classes.name: org-name-requires-legal-suffix
fn_classes.mechanism: ORGANIZATION requires a legal suffix (Inc/Corp/LLC/...); suffix-less brand names ('Verdant Goods') are missed outright or captured as PERSON_NAME ('Harrison & Associates Advertising' → partial PERSON span, wrong label).
examples: <<Verdant Goods>> is proud to present our latest product (PERSON_NAME fired, maps to first_name — FN for company_name)
<<Harrison & Associates Advertising>> has been tasked with creating (PERSON_NAME subspan IoU 0.667)
fn_classes.remediation: Labeled-field capture ('Company Name:' licenses the value) + '&/and Sons/Associates'-style org-internal markers + NER org label via fusion; also arbitration: an org-shaped span should shadow PERSON_NAME (the arbitration exists but only fires when ORGANIZATION itself detects).

fn_classes.name: bare-address-component (trailing ZIP, tabular city)
fn_classes.mechanism: Address components without their own label: ZIP as the trailing element of 'City, ST 85705' (cue is the ADDRESS SHAPE, not a 'zip' word), city names in table cells or 'the city of San Antonio' (preposition between cue and value).
examples: I reside at 35 Old Manor Rd, Tucson, AZ <<85705>> (ADDRESS matched only the street part, IoU 0.152)
operates in the city of <<San Antonio>> ('of' breaks LOCATION_CONTEXT adjacency)
| 200 Allandale Rd | <<Brandon>> | USA | (table cell, no inline cue)
fn_classes.remediation: Address-shape composite pattern: '<street>, <City>, <ST> <5-digit>' emitting sub-spans for city/state/zip; plus table-header-aware field capture (column header carries the label).

fn_classes.name: dob-scored-as-generic-date
fn_classes.mechanism: DATE_ISO finds the exact DOB span (IoU 1.0) but the 1:1 label projection sends it to 'date' while gold says date_of_birth; the context-cued DATE_OF_BIRTH pattern that would win fails through markdown ('**Date of Birth**: 2005-07-01') and prose ('born on'). Twin FP class date-on-date_of_birth (158).
examples: - **Date of Birth**: <<2005-07-01>> (DATE_ISO hit, DOB cue blocked by '**:')
I, Donald, born on <<2001-01-08>> ('born on' cue not bridged)
fn_classes.remediation: Same shared cue-bridge fix as the adjacency class (DOB cue + markdown tolerance); type arbitration: a date span within reach of a DOB cue upgrades DATE→DATE_OF_BIRTH.

fn_classes.name: label-map-collision (fax-as-phone, ipv6-to-ipv4)
fn_classes.mechanism: fax_number gold (84): our PHONE_NUMBER correctly finds the number but there is no native FAX type, so it scores FP-on-fax + FN. ipv6 gold (29): IP_ADDRESS detects many IPv6 values but the 1:1 map projects IP_ADDRESS→ipv4 only, leaving ipv6 unreachable (17 of the 29 were actually detected).
examples: Fax: <<951-708-7546>> (found as PHONE_NUMBER; no fax label to map to)
ipv6 gold overlapped by our IP_ADDRESS prediction — scored FN purely by the 1:1 projection
fn_classes.remediation: Not-fixable at pattern level: either add a FAX subtype (cue 'Fax:') and split IP into v4/v6 native labels, or accept as an honest projection cost.

fn_classes.name: gold-noise-placeholder-values
fn_classes.mechanism: Gold annotates blank form placeholders and label-text as PII values: runs of underscores ('_______' as postcode/loan fields, 16 spans) and header text ('Temporary Password', 'secure password' as password values, 3 spans).
examples: - Loan Type: <<___________________________>> (gold span is the blank line)
**<<Temporary Password>>:** b9M!k7Lp#5nXz3 (gold marks the LABEL, and separately the value)
register... using their email address and a <<secure password>> (descriptive phrase, no secret present)
fn_classes.remediation: Not fixable — do not chase; exclude from any tuned re-run's error budget.

fp_classes.name: titlecase-phrase-as-person
fp_classes.mechanism: PERSON_FULL_NAME is a bare capitalized-bigram matcher; it fires on markdown headers and field labels ('Personal Information', 'Security Instructions', 'Registration Form'), Title-Case geo names ('Hays County', 'Fresno County'), suffix-less org names, and Title-Case occupations ('Customer Service Representative'). 5,659 of 6,324 PERSON_NAME FPs are Title-Case multi-word; 2,627 sit directly against markdown header/label markers; 5,270 overlap NO gold at all. Dominant FP class: 71% of all FPs.
examples: residing in <<Hays County>> (gold county, IoU 1.0, labeled first_name by us)
the account holder resides is <<Fresno County>>
fp_classes.remediation: Document-structure awareness: suppress bare-bigram PERSON inside markdown headers/bold field labels (offset-preserving structure pass); common-noun/section-word stoplist for the bigram matcher; geo-gazetteer + 'County/Bank/Services'-tail arbitration. Highest-leverage single precision fix in the library; recurs on ANY markdown/form corpus.

fp_classes.name: split-name-convention-FP
fp_classes.mechanism: Twin of the FN class: the correct full-name span fails IoU 0.5 against the first_name token gold, so the very detection that found the person counts as an FP.
fp_classes.remediation: Same as FN twin: component sub-span emission; convention, not a bug.

fp_classes.name: gps-pattern-on-numeric-pairs
fp_classes.mechanism: GPS_COORDINATES accepts '/' as the lat/long separator with no context requirement, so it fires on dd/mm inside dates ('15/09'/2026 — 321 FPs land on date gold), ratings ('4.5/5'), availability ('24/7'), and comma-grouped money ('1,125.00').
fp_classes.remediation: Drop '/' as a separator (or require a coordinate cue/hemisphere/degree marker); range-check both components only helps partially since dd/mm passes. Add the 'lat, long' context guard the FN side also needs ('40.7234 N, 123.1235 W').

fp_classes.name: date-taxonomy-split-FP
fp_classes.mechanism: Our DATE matches the date portion of datetimes and birthdates; Nemotron splits date_time and date_of_birth from date, so correct format detections score as label-mismatch FPs (184 on date_time, 158 on date_of_birth).
examples: timestamp gold date_time '2025-11-07T18:00:00' — our DATE_ISO hit scores FP
**Date of Birth**: 1990-03-22 — DATE hit, date_of_birth gold
fp_classes.remediation: Projection artifact; partially recoverable via DOB-cue arbitration (see FN dob class). Not a masking-safety problem (the value IS masked).

fp_classes.name: cue-captures-following-label-word
fp_classes.mechanism: Cue-gated patterns with IGNORECASE alnum value classes and optional separators capture the NEXT ENGLISH WORD when the real value is held off by punctuation: USERNAME grabs 'Account' from 'User Account...', MEDICAL_RECORD grabs the literal word 'number' from 'medical record number, LAC-00132857', and 'patient id' matches INSIDE 'Patient Identification' capturing 'entification'.
examples: Your medical record <<number>>, LAC-00132857 ([A-Z0-9]{4,20} + IGNORECASE matches 'number')
**Patient Id<<entification>>** (cue matched mid-word; no boundary after 'id')
fp_classes.remediation: Require word boundary after the cue token; case-sensitive or shape-checked value classes (must contain a digit for id types); negative lookahead for the label's own continuation words. Precision twin of the FN adjacency class — the same shared bridge component should carry both.

fp_classes.name: digit-run-inside-larger-identifier
fp_classes.mechanism: Numeric patterns fire on digit substrings of longer prefixed identifiers: PHONE_NUMBER on the 10-digit tail of 'BIO-7485236911' (biometric) and of customer/MRN ids; bare 9-digit US_SSN on 9-digit customer_ids ('347258916'); CREDIT_CARD on 16-digit hyphenated account numbers.
fp_classes.remediation: Left-context guard: suppress numeric matches immediately preceded by '[A-Z]+-' or an alnum prefix; competing-cue arbitration (a 'customer id'/'biometric' cue within range outbids bare SSN/phone). Generic mechanism — recurs wherever composite IDs embed digit runs.

fp_classes.name: org-on-headers-or-unannotated-gold
fp_classes.mechanism: ORGANIZATION FPs split two ways: Title-Case section headers ('Transaction Services', 'Disability Insurance Terms') — same header mechanism as the person class — and genuinely-correct organizations gold never annotated ('First National Bank' as Lender, twice), i.e. partial annotation noise.
examples: Lender: <<First National Bank>> (real org, unannotated in gold)
fp_classes.remediation: Header suppression handles the first half; the unannotated-real-org half is gold noise — don't tune against it.

fp_classes.name: age-span-shape-and-cohort-ranges
fp_classes.mechanism: 74/88 are boundary convention: our AGE span includes unit words ('42 year old', 'aged 76') vs gold's bare number '42' (IoU<0.3 → FP+FN pair). 14/88 fire on non-personal cohort/eligibility ranges ('Age 25-45', 'at least 18 years old').
examples: Melissa Thornton, a <<42 year old>> female (gold '42', IoU 0.18)
Be at least <<18 years old>> on or before the next election (eligibility rule)
fp_classes.remediation: Emit the numeric sub-span as the canonical AGE span (keep the phrase as evidence); suppress when followed by a range dash or inside eligibility/'between X and Y' frames.

fp_classes.name: fax-as-phone-FP
fp_classes.mechanism: PHONE_NUMBER correctly matches fax numbers; fax_number is a distinct gold type with no native counterpart — every hit is an automatic label-mismatch FP (pairs with the FN class).
fp_classes.remediation: 'Fax:' cue subtype or accept as projection cost; the value is still masked correctly in production.

fp_classes.name: nested-entity-and-ip-version-projection
fp_classes.mechanism: IP-inside-URL: we emit the inner IPv4 of 'http://192.168.1.100:8080/...' while gold annotates the whole URL (nested-entity convention, 28). IPv6 values we detect score as ipv4 FPs against ipv6 gold because the 1:1 map has only IP_ADDRESS→ipv4 (17 vanilla / 22 swarm).
examples: our IPv6 detection scored against ipv6 gold as an ipv4-label FP
fp_classes.remediation: Nested-span containment credit at eval time; split native IP into v4/v6 labels. Both are projection/convention, not detection errors.

fp_classes.name: residual-spurious (incl. swarm-only engine noise)
fp_classes.mechanism: Long tail: DATE_ISO/DATE_TIME on odd numerics, LOCATION 'from <Word>' captures, LICENSE_PLATE on random alnum after 'tag'. The swarm's +25 here are its only behavioral FP delta: non-regex engines emit DATE_TIME on malformed id-like numerics ('1526-32-18-49' — a medical record number) and gliner window-offset name fragments ('Col<<leen Redding>>' — span starts mid-word, a windowing/offset anchoring bug worth checking in the adapter).
examples: medical record number <<1526-32-18-49>> → DATE_TIME (swarm-only, engine date parser)
Col<<leen Redding>> (swarm-only PERSON_NAME with mid-word start — offset anchoring)
fp_classes.remediation: Plausibility gate on fused non-regex findings (calendar-valid dates; word-boundary check on span starts — the mid-word start is a cheap universal validity filter).

result.swarm_delta_note: Swarm is behaviorally ~identical to vanilla on Nemotron: FN 6966→6961 (5 fixed — 3 single-token first names in prose ("Meet <<Adam>>", "Meet <<Jane>>", "While <<Jorge>> showed") and 2 phone formats; 0 FNs introduced), FP 8306→8348 (+42 swarm-only: 26 DATE_TIME on malformed numeric ids like "1526-32-18-49", 7 PERSON_NAME incl. the mid-word-anchored "Col<<leen Redding>>", 5 ipv4, 3 ssn incl. "1,500"; 0 vanilla FPs removed). The gliner pre-fusion probe (30 prose records, GLiNERAdapter run directly vs the fused swarm output) explains why: gliner emitted 124 findings; 69 (56%) are absent from the fused output; 26 of the discarded spans hit reachable gold at IoU 1.0 — passwords behind "**Temporary Password:**" (b9M!k7Lp#5nXz3), usernames behind "**User ID:**" (zakaria.ramos, b.puckett), DOBs after "born on" (2001-01-08), and single-token first names (Donald, Julio) — i.e. precisely the top regex FN classes (adjacency-broken labeled values and single-token names). The floor-projecting swarm fusion discards gliner-only findings instead of admitting them, so the ensemble recovers almost none of gliner's complementary recall. Additional recoverable mass is span-right/label-wrong: discarded gliner NATIONAL_ID spans on biometric_identifier gold and PASSWORD on pin/swift_bic values — a fusion policy that accepts high-confidence gliner SPANS and re-arbitrates the TYPE from local cues would convert both groups. This is the single clearest fusion-behavior finding: the recall headroom exists pre-fusion and is being thrown away post-fusion.
result.gold_noise_note: Gold noise is small and quantified: 16/6966 FN gold spans are blank form placeholders (runs of underscores annotated as postcode/loan-field values) and 3 are label-text-as-value ("Temporary Password", "secure password" annotated as password secrets) — together <0.3% of FNs. On the FP side, some spans we flag are genuinely correct but unannotated in gold (e.g. Lender "First National Bank" never marked company_name — a slice of the 328 ORGANIZATION FPs), and the adapter's documented taxonomy quirks stand: tax_id gold mixes SSN-formatted values (our ssn hits score as FPs), fax_number is split from phone_number, ipv6 unreachable under the 1:1 ipv4 map. Net: Nemotron gold is substantially clean; the failure mass is dominated by real capability gaps (Title-Case-as-person FPs, cue-adjacency FNs) and label-projection conventions, not annotation noise. Nothing here justifies chasing gold-noise classes in remediation, and any cue-synonym/value-format lexicons proposed above must be derived from the upstream TRAIN parquet (only test-00000-of-00001.parquet is currently local under pii-anon-eval-data/external_eval/data/nemotron/).

result.dataset: gretelai/synthetic_pii_finance_multilingual (English_test) via ds_gretel.py — seeded subsample(SEED=20260710) cap=1200 of 2891; relaxed matching (IoU>=0.5 same mapped label). Sample-level relaxed: vanilla tp=2697 fp=11601 fn=2563 (P=0.189 R=0.513); swarm tp=2809 fp=11973 fn=2451 (P=0.190 R=0.534) — matches the recorded full-split runs. KEY REFRAME of the briefing question: the FP spray is NOT concentrated in the structured formats — fixed-field docs (SWIFT/MT940/BAI/FIX/EDI/CSV/XBRL/FpML/ISDA) hold only 13.9% of FPs and actually score HIGHER precision (P=0.210 R=0.410) than prose/forms (P=0.185 R=0.538). The precision killer is corpus-wide: 71% of ALL FPs are PERSON_NAME on Title-Case financial vocabulary. The structured formats instead drive the RECALL side (ALL-CAPS values, bare tag values, single-token CSV cells).

fn_classes.name: suffixless-topographic street-address grammar
fn_classes.mechanism: _ADDRESS requires a closed US street-suffix list (Street/Ave/Rd/...); 1573/2194 gold addresses in the full split have NO listed suffix (Faker-style 'number + name + arbitrary topographic noun' — Harbors/Keys/Vista/Row/Run — plus Apt./Suite/Flat tails and international forms), and gold spans extend through unit/floor/city/postcode so even suffix-hits fail IoU>=0.5 (93 additional strict-only boundary FPs). Identical in swarm because the Layer-4 corroboration gate discards single-engine gliner ADDRESS findings (see swarm_delta_note).
examples: registered office at <<4th Floor, 123 Regent Street, London, W1B 5EE>>
fn_classes.remediation: Open the address grammar: house-number + 1-4 capitalized tokens + OPTIONAL suffix, with optional unit/city/postcode tail; and (bigger win) let corroboration-gated gliner ADDRESS findings survive fusion — gliner already finds these (44/60 sampled fusion-discards were street_address).

fn_classes.name: org name without legal suffix / ALL-CAPS org
fn_classes.mechanism: ORGANIZATION patterns are suffix/industry-noun/camelcase/context gated; plain multi-word brands ('Synthetic Tech', 'World Bank', 'GlobalBank' — 2006/3476 gold have no legal suffix) and ALL-CAPS headers are unreachable. Swarm adds exactly 0: gliner's _PII_LABELS has no organization/company label and presidio's ORG label is not in the adapter output mapping, so no pooled engine emits ORGANIZATION at all.
examples: CARRIER: <<Oceanus Shipping Lines, Inc.>> (has suffix, still missed)
fn_classes.remediation: Add 'organization'/'company' to GLiNERAdapter._PII_LABELS (+_LABEL_MAP) and map presidio ORG — the single cheapest recall capability on this class; regex side: allow comma-before-suffix ('Lines, Inc.') and ALL-CAPS org form after party-role labels (CARRIER:/Issued by:).

fn_classes.name: name-shape coverage (non-ASCII, hyphenated, single-token, ALL-CAPS, labeled-value adjacency)
fn_classes.mechanism: PERSON_NAME token class is ASCII [A-Z][a-z]+: diacritics truncate ('Linda Bostr' from 'Linda Boström'), hyphenated surnames split ('Anna Jennings'), ALL-CAPS registers (SWIFT :50K:/:59:, BAI) never match, single-token given names (quoted CSV cells, salutations) have no pattern, and the trailing field-label window suppresses real labeled values ('Name: John Doe\nPolicy Number:' — probe-verified miss). Sub-counts (van): multi-token-missed 193, single-token 136, non-ASCII 87, allcaps 52, hyphen 15.
fn_classes.remediation: Unicode letter classes (\p{Lu}\p{Ll}-equivalent) with internal hyphen/apostrophe joins; ALL-CAPS name path gated to labeled/party fields; stop the field-label trailing window from consuming across line breaks; lexicon-gated single-token names inside delimited (CSV/pipe) cells.

fn_classes.name: unreachable gold types under one-to-one label projection
fn_classes.mechanism: The adapter's one-label-per-native-type map cannot reach gretel's time (88), first_name (84), customer_id (36), last_name (32), date_time (18), ipv6 (18). ipv6/date_time are detected natively but mapped elsewhere; first/last_name are a span-convention split of full names; TIME and a generic customer-id class genuinely don't exist as native types.
fn_classes.remediation: Eval-side: allow one-to-many pred_map (IP_ADDRESS->{ipv4,ipv6}, PERSON_NAME->{name,first_name,last_name}). Library-side: a TIME native type and a generic labeled CUSTOMER/ACCOUNT-ID type are real gaps; the rest is scoring convention, not detection.

fn_classes.name: keyword-gated ID/value types: value-shape whitelist too narrow + keywordless fixed-field values
fn_classes.mechanism: Two sub-mechanisms: (a) the labeled-value capture group is narrower than real ID shapes — 'Employee ID: T-403906-V' missed because the pattern only accepts EMP-\d+ or bare digits (probe-verified); 'BBAN: KALL90112673253892' missed though the keyword is literally present; (b) fixed-field formats carry bare values under standard tags with no English keyword (':71A:M6884451'). Covers employee_id 43, bban 31, bank_routing 23, passport 22, drivers_license 17, cvv 16, password 15, swift_bic 15, pin 12, dob 12, api_key 12.
fn_classes.remediation: Widen labeled-value shapes to generic alphanumeric-with-dashes tokens after a matched keyword (keyword gate keeps precision); add industry-standard structured-message field-tag gating (SWIFT MT :50K:/:59:/:71A:, EDI segments) mapping tag->entity-type — format-aware but standard-based, not dataset anchors.

fn_classes.name: date/time grammar gaps (day-first, legal long-form, tz-datetimes)
fn_classes.mechanism: DATE grammar covers month-name-first and slashed numeric only; day-first ('15-Jan-2023', '1st of April'), legal long-form ('1st day of January, 2023'), weekday-prefixed, and space-separated datetime-with-tz forms all miss (153 day-first gold in the full split).
examples: dated as of the <<1st day of January, 2023>>
fn_classes.remediation: Add day-first (d-MMM-yyyy, 'Nth of Month'), ordinal-legal, and 'yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss TZ' sub-patterns to the DATE/DATETIME family.

fn_classes.name: phone format gaps (parenthesized-area + dotted + extensions)
fn_classes.mechanism: Vanilla misses '(123) 456-7890' after 'Contact Number:' and dotted/extension forms '714.660.1941 x2744' (probe-verified). This is the one class the swarm genuinely closes: presidio PHONE_NUMBER recovers 79 of 91 (relaxed; strict full-split +178 tp).
fn_classes.remediation: Port the missing surface forms into the regex layer (parenthesized area code without keyword-adjacency requirements, dotted separators, x-extensions) so the vanilla path doesn't depend on presidio for NANP basics.

fn_classes.name: placeholder/template gold spans
fn_classes.mechanism: Gold labels literal template placeholders as PII: bracketed slots, underscore blanks, format masks. No detector should find these; also role nouns labeled name/company ('safety inspector', 'customer service department', 'Complainant') sit inside the name:multi-token bucket.
examples: <<[Tenant's Full Name]>>, residing at [Rental Property Address]
fn_classes.remediation: Not fixable — dataset noise; exclude placeholder-shaped gold (^\[|^_+|MM/DD) from any tuned-eval variant and document.

fp_classes.name: Title-Case form-label/heading phrase as PERSON_NAME
fp_classes.mechanism: THE precision killer (71% of all FPs, both detectors). The bare 2-3-token Title-Case full-name regex fires on financial form labels, section headings, and table row labels; the closed _FIELD_LABEL_NOUNS deny list (Number/Code/Account/...) covers a tiny fraction of the financial label vocabulary — Charge, Balance, Amount, Price, Endorsements, Compliance, Assets, Services, Period all uncovered. Faker city names ('West Kimberly', 'North Luishaven') and determiner-phrases ('The Insurer') also hit. 25-sample audit: overwhelmingly junk even in records where name IS a declared/annotated type (only 4874/8270 are in name-declared records, and those are still 'Waiting Period'-class matches).
fp_classes.remediation: Replace the closed deny-noun list with a mechanism: (a) corpus-frequency common-English-word filter on both tokens (derivable from English_train or any prose corpus — legal under tuning discipline); (b) for context-free bare matches require a given-name-lexicon hit on token 1; (c) suppress matches immediately followed by ':'/'|' or inside markdown '**'/table-cell delimiters (form-label position).

fp_classes.name: unlabeled real PII of undeclared types (partial-annotation gold)
fp_classes.mechanism: Gold is limited per-record to the declared pii_types list (verified: 2891/2891 records; 45.3%/44.4% of ALL FPs are on undeclared types). Correct detections of real emails, dates, addresses, phones in a record that didn't declare that type score as FPs. Count here = the real-PII-shaped portion: date 1108/1206 (every doc carries operational dates; sampled UNDECL date FPs are all real dates), email 247 (all real addresses; includes markdown '[x](mailto:x)' double-hits where gold covers one leg), street_address 163, phone 35/49.
examples: Email: [<<heinz.henck@email.com>>](mailto:...) — email not a declared type
fp_classes.remediation: Not fixable at the detector; for honest benchmarking score each record only on its declared types (report as a separate metrics row). Detector-side nit that IS fixable: emit one span for markdown link-text/mailto duplicates.

fp_classes.name: GPS decimal-pair on money amounts and date fragments
fp_classes.mechanism: _GPS matches ANY two in-range numbers around ','/'/': thousands-separated amounts ('88,126' parses as lat 88, lon 126), dd/mm fragments ('01/10'), and rate pairs all qualify — mapped to local_latlng these are 1698 FPs on the full split (P=0.013). Probe-verified: '$88,126' and '12.5/25.0' both fire.
fp_classes.remediation: Require coordinate-plausible precision (both components with >=3 decimal places) OR an adjacent coordinate keyword (lat/long/GPS/coordinates); reject when preceded by a currency symbol or inside a d/m/y date continuation.

fp_classes.name: industry-noun Title-Case heading as ORGANIZATION
fp_classes.mechanism: The industry-noun ORGANIZATION pattern accepts any Title-Case phrase headed by Insurance/Services/etc., so policy-document section headings and coverage-type lists match as company names.
fp_classes.remediation: Reject candidates in heading/list positions (preceded by list markers 'a.'/'1.'/'**', followed by ':'), require an org-evidencing context (at/with/by + phrase, or legal suffix) for industry-noun matches.

fp_classes.name: bare 9/10-digit numerics as SSN/phone in structured registers
fp_classes.mechanism: The no-separator US_SSN pattern (9 digits) and permissive phone matching fire on CAS numbers, FIX tag values, MT940 statement references, and invoice/account numerics that saturate machine formats — ssn 187/194 (full-split ssn P=0.164), phone 43/60.
fp_classes.remediation: Keyword-gate the no-separator SSN form (SSN/social security within window — the dashed forms stay ungated); inside key:value/tag-register lines require phone punctuation shape or a phone keyword before emitting PHONE_NUMBER.

fp_classes.name: swarm-added engine FPs: gliner name fragments + presidio date phrase-extents
fp_classes.mechanism: All net-new swarm FPs (364 new + label shifts): gliner emits truncated name fragments at hyphen/initial boundaries ('Engelbert Kohl' from 'Kohl-Debes', 'Albert V.' from 'Albert V. Ferguson') that fail IoU 0.5; presidio DATE_TIME includes leading phrase words ('the Year Ended December 31, 2021', 'no later than March 20, 2023') so a real date scores FP+FN. Full-split strict: date +249 FP, name +35 FP.
fp_classes.remediation: Fusion-level boundary normalization: strip leading stopwords/determiners from DATE_TIME spans; extend NER name spans across internal hyphens to the full token run before clustering.

fp_classes.name: USERNAME keyword-adjacency grabs ordinary words
fp_classes.mechanism: The USERNAME context pattern accepts any capitalized token after 'User'/'User:' — 'User Information:', 'User reported', and first names after 'User:' all emit user_name FPs in support-ticket registers.
fp_classes.remediation: Require handle-like value shape (contains digit/underscore/dot, or all-lowercase, no interior space) for USERNAME captures; plain capitalized dictionary words should not qualify.

fp_classes.name: label-projection granularity FPs (ipv6-as-ipv4, keyword-gated account digits as bban)
fp_classes.mechanism: Documented adapter choices, not detector errors: our single IP type maps to ipv4 so correct IPv6 detections (28) score as ipv4 FPs; keyword-gated BANK_ACCOUNT digit captures (39, real account numbers 'Account Number: 12345678') map to bban whose gretel shape is 4 letters + 14 digits.
examples: IP Address: <<fb6f:5bea:a35e:...:4f2b>> scored as ipv4 FP
Account Number: <<12345678>> scored as bban FP
fp_classes.remediation: Eval-side one-to-many mapping fixes ipv6; the bban mismatch argues for a distinct BBAN-shaped sub-pattern (4 alpha + 14 digit) inside BANK_ACCOUNT — that one IS a small general capability add (31 FNs close too).

fp_classes.name: ALL-CAPS English word as SWIFT_BIC
fp_classes.mechanism: _SWIFT_BIC = [A-Z]{4}[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{2}([A-Z0-9]{3})? matches any 8- or 11-letter uppercase token, so ordinary words in caps registers (SWIFT bodies, headers) qualify — probe-verified 'CUSTOMER' and 'INTEREST' fire. 52 FPs on the full split (P=0.577).
fp_classes.remediation: Validate positions 5-6 against the ISO-3166 country-code set AND require either a BIC/SWIFT keyword in-window or a known bank-code prefix; a small English-word deny list catches the residue.

result.swarm_delta_note: Swarm differs on exactly 4 types (full-split strict delta: name +691 tp/+35 fp from gliner; phone +178 tp/+42 fp from presidio; ssn +8/+11; date +11/+249 from presidio DATE_TIME) — every other type byte-identical because gliner has no org/address-adjacent labels mapped that survive, and presidio PERSON is dropped by PRED_MAP (only PERSON_NAME is mapped). On my n=1200 relaxed sample: +112 tp (phone 79, name ~25, ssn 5) vs +372 fp (gliner name fragments 242, presidio date extents 98). Under RELAXED scoring the swarm's name gain nearly vanishes (FN 483 to 458) because vanilla already relaxed-matched what gliner strict-fixes — gliner's real contribution is exact boundaries (boundary-only strict-FPs drop 834 to 592). GLINER-FOUND-BUT-FUSION-DISCARDED (prose probe, 150 records, 780 gold): gliner alone relaxed-matched 408 gold; the fused swarm output matched 427; but 152 gold spans gliner matched were LOST post-fusion (sampled 60: street_address 44, name 13, passport/dob/phone 1 each). Mechanism: ADDRESS and PERSON_NAME are SEMANTIC_TYPES behind the Layer-4 corroboration gate (need 2 engines or meta-score >= 0.85); regex never corroborates suffixless addresses, and FloorProjectingFusion re-injects only regex-oss spans, so single-engine gliner findings die. Letting corroboration-gated gliner ADDRESS findings through (or adding gliner to the floor for ADDRESS) is the single highest-leverage fusion change measured on this dataset — it attacks the largest FN class (726 street_address).
result.gold_noise_note: Three distinct noise mechanisms, all measured: (1) PARTIAL ANNOTATION BY DESIGN — every record's gold is limited to its declared pii_types list (verified 2891/2891; 338 records declare zero types), so real unlabeled PII of undeclared types scores as FP: 45.3% of vanilla FPs (5254/11601) and 44.4% of swarm FPs are on undeclared types; sampled undeclared email/date/address FPs are essentially all real PII. Any precision number on this dataset is therefore a floor; per-record declared-type scoring is the honest variant. (2) TEMPLATE PLACEHOLDERS AS GOLD — '[Tenant's Full Name]', '______________', 'MM/DD/YYYY', '[Date]', '[(XXX) XXX-XXXX]' (~200 spans full-split; 62 FNs in my sample) are unfindable by design. (3) ROLE/DESCRIPTION NOUNS AS GOLD — 'safety inspector', 'Complainant', 'Non-notifying Party' labeled name; 'customer service department' labeled company (~85 spans full-split). Additionally the dataset counts generic dates/times as PII and includes bracket/key-prefix characters in some gold extents ('[support@invoicingplatform.com]'), which strict penalizes and relaxed partially absorbs.

result.dataset: TAB/ECHR echr_test via ds_tab.py — all 127 real court judgments, 7160 gold spans (union-of-annotators maskable set); scored strict + relaxed(IoU>=0.5 same-label) per common.py; mechanism mining joined at strict with tier diagnostics (boundary/partial/label-confusion/missed)

fn_classes.name: prose-date-not-in-pattern-repertoire
fn_classes.mechanism: DATE_ISO/DATE_TIME natives match numeric/ISO forms only; natural-language dates (day-Month-year, Month-year, date ranges) never fire. 2159 pure prose-date shapes + 81 mixed forms = 79-82% of ALL DATETIME gold. Fully within pattern reach (a month-name date grammar); presidio, already in the swarm pool, hits DATETIME relaxed recall 0.918 solo.
examples: On <<27 May 1994>> the applicant submitted his final observations
In March 1993, <<September 1993>> and March 1994 the applicants contacted the Court of Appeal
fn_classes.remediation: Add a natural-language date pattern family to DATE_TIME (day-Month-year, Month-year, 'Month d, yyyy', ranges); independently, fix fusion so presidio DATE_TIME (already native-named) survives — either lever closes most of the class.

fn_classes.name: bare-year-quasi-identifier
fn_classes.mechanism: A lone 4-digit year is maskable gold in TAB (mostly birth years). 149/302 sit in an explicit 'born in <year>' context — pattern-reachable as a DATE_OF_BIRTH context grammar; the other 153 are free-standing years whose identifying force needs document-level reasoning (firing on every year would be precision-suicidal).
examples: from 4 at the end of <<1985>> to 3,205 at the end of January 1987
who was born in <<1987>> and is currently in detention
fn_classes.remediation: Contextual 'born in/on YYYY' DATE_OF_BIRTH pattern for the reachable half; leave free-standing years to a future document-level maskability layer — do not pattern-chase them.

fn_classes.name: duration-relative-time-expression
fn_classes.mechanism: TAB DATETIME includes durations ('three days', '9 years'' imprisonment'); no native type covers elapsed-time expressions. Surface shape (number|spelled-number + time-unit) is pattern-reachable; whether a duration is identifying is quasi/doc-level.
examples: extend the custody period for <<three days>>
he was sentenced to 12 months' imprisonment
fn_classes.remediation: New DURATION capability (number+unit grammar) exposed as an opt-in quasi-identifier type; only worth shipping if a doc-level or policy layer decides maskability.

fn_classes.name: institution-name-consumed-by-person-heuristic
fn_classes.mechanism: ORG gold overlapped only by PERSON_NAME predictions: the capitalized-token-run person pattern eats multiword institution names ('Katowice Regional Court', 'Army Board'). Largest single ORG failure and the FN face of the 667-count FP class below — one mechanism, both directions.
examples: On 6 September 2000 the <<Katowice Regional Court (Sąd Okręgowy)>> held the first hearing (pred: PERSON_NAME)
On 8 June 2000 the <<Gaziantep Administrative Court>> decided
fn_classes.remediation: Institution-keyword arbitration in the existing eval_cross_type_arbitration seam: a capitalized run containing Court/Ministry/Board/Commission/Directorate/etc. demotes PERSON_NAME and emits ORGANIZATION; generalizes to any formal-document corpus.

fn_classes.name: unmodeled-institution-org
